source.title: Eliciting Numerical Predictive Distributions of LLMs Without Autoregression
source.authors: Julianna Piskorz; Katarzyna Kobalczyk; M. van der Schaar

page_placements.theme: Response-level properties of the upcoming output encoded before or early in generation

record.tranche_reason: The study trains probes on the final input-token representations to predict statistics and quantiles of the next numerical output, testing future-output decodability with a different method and in a numerical forecasting setting. It does not intervene on the representation to test whether it causally shapes intervening tokens.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the reported point-prediction probe results, its reported magnitude accuracy and correlations, and quantile-probe results for the predictive distribution. The paper also reports downstream ground-truth forecasting error, efficiency, layer ablations, and broader generalisation results; these do not directly measure the future-output information in the representation as specified by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper probes final-input-position hidden states of five open LLMs (last 8 layers concatenated) to recover the full next number before decoding. For Llama-2 that number spans several digit tokens, so this tests V2 multi-token decodability in a new setting, numerical time-series forecasting. It has no interventions and no rhyme or other planning tasks.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that hidden states encode point predictions and uncertainty of the numeric output before decoding, and that much numerical 'reasoning' happens during input processing. They also state that cross-dataset generalisation is limited, that probes are model-specific, and that sampling-based targets are a costly, imperfect proxy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses supervised magnitude-factorised regression and quantile probes on final input-token representations to recover numerical outputs and distribution summaries; it does not use a future-token lens or causal interventions on generation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported IQR correlations vary with dataset scale; generalisation and interval coverage vary with training/test data regime. The paper also reports that layer choice and concatenating multiple layers affect probe performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Quantile probes on final-position hidden states recover the spread of the LLM's sampled numeric outputs (IQR Spearman about 0.90) and give near-nominal interval coverage in-distribution. Coverage degrades under sub-dataset and synthetic-to-real shift.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hidden states before decoding encode the uncertainty/spread of a model's multi-token output distribution.

record.problems: The evidence is based on supervised probes trained against LLM outputs rather than causal interventions. The main experiments use synthetic time series and the probe is model-specific; the authors note that empirical sampling is an imperfect and computationally costly proxy. The tested numerical forecasting setup does not establish token-level look-ahead or causal effects on intervening text.
record.rows_left_out: Section 4, Table 3 and Figure 4 report ground-truth forecasting error and sample efficiency rather than direct measures of future-output information in the representation. Section 5.1 Figure 5 reports context-length generalisation; Figure 6 reports median-prediction errors by real-world sub-dataset; Appendix C.2 Tables 11 and Figures 7–10 report additional model results; Appendix C.4 Figures 11–12 report layer ablations; Appendix C.5 Table 13 reports quantile absolute errors. These are omitted as redundant or as downstream/generalisation results not directly measuring the version's core future-output decodability.

untested.parts: Prediction of specific tokens at specified offsets. Single-layer decodability (the main probes concatenate 8 layers; single layers appear only in the ablation). Non-numeric text.
All: no rhyming verse, no frontier model, no interventions.
All: no test of whether features are computed for later positions rather than as a by-product of next-token prediction.
All: no rhyme planning or attribution-graph analysis.
Numeric decodability is shown, but there is no evidence of a look-ahead mechanism that steers generation, and no reasoning, chess or Sokoban tasks.
All: no causal test of whether the decodable information steers generation or reflects local input features.

missing.what: Combined-scale log-scale correlations for the other four models: mean 0.98-0.99, median 0.90-0.97, greedy 0.62-0.91 (DeepSeek greedy 0.62, Llama-3-8B 0.79, Llama-3.2-3B 0.76, Phi 0.91).

Single-layer probes (layers 16-32) perform worse than the 8-layer concatenation, which bears on 'single hidden state'. Greedy information is concentrated in the last layers; mean information peaks at layer 30.
Vanilla MLP probes give 33-42% higher MSE than the factorised probe, so measured decodability depends on probe design.

record.verdict_notes: Probes use the final input position but concatenate 8 layers, not a single vector. Targets for mean, median and quantiles are sample statistics, not specific tokens; the greedy target is the closest analogue to V2. Baselines are naive input heuristics, not a control probe on input embeddings, so the study cannot separate plan-like information from input-derived forecastability. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse prompts, candidate rhyme representations, or interventions changing a rhyme word or line.

Tests recovery of numerical output statistics and distributional summaries from concatenated hidden states at the final input position, not prediction of specified future tokens at specified offsets from a single hidden-state vector. Does not test whether the representation causally shapes intervening text.
No causal test distinguishing features computed to assist later positions from features arising as a by-product of next-token prediction.
No rhyme-planning test or open attribution-graph/probing-tool analysis. Use of open-weight models on numerical forecasting does not test this version.
No multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or other non-verse look-ahead task.
Does not test whether apparent plans are shallow, local next-token features, or heuristics that fail to steer generation.

relation.reason: Its own probing experiments test whether input-position representations encode numerical outputs before autoregressive generation.

tranche.reason: The study tests pre-decoding recovery of multi-token numerical outputs in the new setting of time-series forecasting.

source_check.notes: Main probes concatenate eight layers at one position; these results are scalar numerical recovery, without per-token accuracy or a causal planning intervention. Rows r20–r30 correctly have no claim-version link; their states describe uncertainty recovery and calibration.

statements.correction: Table 10, mean/median/greedy MSE: Llama-2 0.006/0.006/0.015; Llama-3 0.007/0.012/0.016; Llama-3.2 0.007/0.013/0.018; Phi-3.5 0.008/0.012/0.020; DeepSeek 0.009/0.013/0.020. Figure 7, other four models: greedy log-scale correlations 0.62–0.91; mean correlations 0.98–0.99. Section 2.2: decoding-by-product explanation is hypothesised.
statements.problem: The roughly 2–3x comparison holds against mean MSE, but not against median MSE in every model. The authors present the decoding explanation as a hypothesis.

statements.correction: Appendix C.1 reports factorised-probe MSE reductions of 41%, 33%, 42% for greedy, mean, median. Table 9, respective MSEs: factorised 0.0150/0.0061/0.0058; vanilla MLP without log-scaling 0.0255/0.0092/0.0100; vanilla MLP with log-scaling 0.0400/0.0091/0.0101.
statements.problem: The 33–42% range describes MSE reductions relative to vanilla MLP, not vanilla MLP increases relative to the factorised probe.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Point-statistic probes for the five reported models on the scale-1.0 synthetic dataset, and Llama-2-7B magnitude and distribution-summary probes in the reported settings
reader_labels.reason: The probes recover LLM point predictions with lower MSE than the simple input baselines (r1–r15); magnitude classification is reported above 90% accurate (r16), and the paper reports strong correlations and near-target interval coverage (r17–r27). This supports numerical-output decodability, not causal steering of intervening text.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Cross-sub-dataset generalisation for the real-data five-fold and synthetic-trained probes
reader_labels.reason: Coverage departs from nominal levels for the Real (5 fold) and Synth settings, especially for the synthetic-trained probe, indicating that recovery is not equally calibrated under these distribution shifts (r29–r30).
